messages:
lee: Heads up — alert from the ingest pipeline: we have a service account key being used unusually often by a batch job. looks like an exposed key pattern: sk-*** in logs. tagging sec oncall.
security-bot: Automated detection: high-volume API key usage (rule: api_key_anomaly_v3). first_seen=1976543187, ip=54.23.12.9, endpoint=/v1/ingest, count=320 in 10m.
sara: Can you paste the log lines (redacted) and which env? staging/prod?
lee: staging only for now. log snippet:
```
2026-10-19T15:06:27Z INFO request api_key=sk-REDACTED service=ingest path=/v1/ingest ip=54.23.12.9 user_agent=batch-runner/1.4.2
2026-10-19T15:07:03Z INFO request api_key=sk-REDACTED service=ingest path=/v1/ingest ip=54.23.12.9
```
alex: if it's a leaked key we should immediately revoke that API key and rotate any SA keys tied to it. also check KMS access logs for recent key unwraps.
morgan: I'll run an audit search across projects for the same api_key fingerprint and check customer-facing routes. can we confirm no production usage yet?
lee: prod shows zero hits for that key. only staging cluster and one ephemeral batch node (batch-worker-7).
sara: @oncall-ops can you suspend batch-worker-7 and block 54.23.12.9 in the firewall while we investigate? :eyes:
oncall-ops: pausing job queue for batch-runner in staging now. added a temporary ip deny for 54.23.12.9. :white_check_mark:
alex: steps I'd take now: 1) disable the API key immediately, 2) revoke any SA key material in the VM metadata if attached, 3) create a replacement scoped key, 4) enforce workload identity for batch jobs. who wants to handle disable?
lee: i'll disable the compromised API key now and post command.
lee: disabling key (GCP/service):
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable $KEY_ID --iam-account=redwood-batch-runner@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
lee: Done — key disabled at 1976543221. Confirmed 0 calls after disable.
security-bot: Alert update: active calls dropped to 0 after key disabled. marking incident: contained.
sara: Good. Morgan — can you pull a timeline of calls and any associated JWT unwrap operations from KMS? need to confirm whether key material was exfiltrated.
morgan: KMS logs show symmetric key unwraps for the batch runner at 1976543100 and 1976543158 from internal GCE. nothing from external IPs. looks like the key was probably copied from a staging VM image snapshot rather than KMS compromise.
alex: important: rotate any VM-level SA keys, and check image build pipelines for accidental inclusion. add a CI scan for embedded keys.
lee: plan for post-incident: 1) rotate affected SA keys and replace with workload identity tokens 2) add repo scan for sk- prefixes 3) add detection rule for repeated calls from single IP to ingest 4) run full bucket/secret scan for staging images
sara: also update audit logging: ensure we maintain detailed logs for the duration and export to long-term storage for analysis. open a ticket to increase retention for staging for 30d.
morgan: tagging a few suspects: build pipeline `batch-image-builder` had an older step that wrote SA keys to /etc/creds. i've started an investigation PR to remove that step.
lee: do we need customer comms? i don't see prod impact. recommend internal postmortem and no customer notification unless we find exfiltration to external party.
alex: +1. Start a quick RCA doc and include scope, timeline, remediation, and follow-ups. assign owners.
sara: owners: remediation (lee), CI/build fix (morgan), detections (alex), audit retention (sara). I'll create the incident ticket and put owners in the assignee list.
oncall-ops: re-enabled batch queue after keys rotated and new token deployed to workers. running health checks.
lee: health checks green. no regressions.
security-bot: Action items created: INC-2026-472 (rotate keys), INC-2026-473 (CI key scan), INC-2026-474 (detection tuning).
morgan: PR to remove key write step is in review: https://git.internal/r/redwood/batch-image-builder/pull/89
sara: Also adding a short privacy/security review: confirm no customer data was processed by those staging jobs in that window.
lee: quick check: data processed was synthetic test payloads only. no PII. will include in RCA.
alex: follow-ups: add RBAC change to disallow long-lived SA keys on build agents, integrate KMS envelope encryption for any persisted creds, and update runbook with these steps.
lee: thanks all — closing thread once tickets are linked in the RCA. :thumbsup:
morgan: closing note: rotate other staging SA keys this week as precaution. :lock:
sara: ok closing — filing postmortem doc now. :spiral_notepad:
